items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: my first teacher, I was recommended through a friend of mine, to a drummer... his name was Charlie Brooks, and I started taking lessons with him

ctx.x: All right, now let's see. During the time that I was doing that outside domestic, outside work, run the elevator, I was friends with a lot of boys that I'd met in New York and we used to fool around. Ukelele was very popular in those days. We used to stand around on the corners and play the ukulele, the Charleston was very popular, we used to get out there and dance and play our ukulele, and believe it or not, I used to dance in those years, they used to have chorus boys like they had chorus girls. Very prominent…

could. Everybody, and of course Bill Robinson was very popular during that time, and I said oh God, it just doesn't take anything, any education at all to get out here and dance, because there's a son of a gun over there that hasn't even been to grade school and can outdance everybody, so then is when I started to study, and my first teacher, I was recommended through a friend of mine, to a drummer that was working in the pit at the Lincoln Theatre in New York, 135th and Lenox Avenue', his name was Charlie…
That's a nice walk for a drummer with all of his equipment.
